items.note: Association, 1889, Larrow Green, 1891 creamery present, but Gideon Vose (bolded) never named in Section A.
Payment by butterfat test not weight is stated (Story 1), but the second bolded element, that the test of the station where he delivers governs, is absent.
'rather than payment by milk weight, making the accuracy of the test crucial to every farmer's monthly income.'
Effie Loomis and Wilbur Teague absent from Section A; only Hobart Sill mentioned in passing.
Selby Vose 'had taken office in 1911' (planted error); not identified as Gideon's son in Section A.
Station-gain ledger line not mentioned anywhere in Section A.
Station, seven miles, 4 May 1896 present; glassware borrowed from Larrow Green (bolded) absent. Story 1 implies it opened with the Ammon outfit.
No composite sample, no percent read on the graduated neck after a fixed pipette charge; only 'test it, separate the cream'.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoiced April 14, 1897; glass in use from 1897 (partial year). Core fact present; 1898 trap avoided.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 cc, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 2: 0.19 'uniform month to month, season to season, wet years and dry'.
Burette mentioned but nothing about a pipette being uncheckable without one or that the county had none.
Tester twenty-nine seasons from opening; dismissed April 30, 1925; died 1934.
Test book only mentioned as the place of the 1911 question mark; bench routine and book's columns and one-hand keeping absent.
Summary leaf not given; 3.61 stated, but 1896 at 3.80 never stated in Section A. Both figures required.
Nine weeks, May 8 to July 10, tests rose and fell back on return of own glass, question mark. 3.80 figure not given, but the core fact is present.
Emmet Brant 'Orra's brother, Ansel's brother-in-law, and the largest patron'.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's own 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) absent; only Ivy's 1958 paraphrase.
'He died in 1934 with the imputation on him.'
Six farms of Hessel Bottom; Emmet Brant the largest.
Weigh book from January 1, 1897 present, but it is described as recording the station's test, and the run never says his scale and the station's agreed.
1902 complaints present, but the Hollow-vs-Green gap is stated as 0.19 (Story 2 and C1b). The key says this conflation loses the item.
Grigg committee 'sampled herds in every season' contradicts January to March 1908 only; also asserts Bulletin 214's 0.20.
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) and the proportional loss absent from Section A.
Roy Brant and the 1958 loan to Ivy absent.
Only 'Rosalie Cudd's cheese factory ledgers from Alder Corners'; no Redlow Ridge, Vessey County or Jerome Cudd.
'the four Hessel Bottom farmers who hauled to the cheese factory in summers 1915-1930'.
Only the artifact (factory ledgers) is named; needs at least two independence elements.
Same four men 'tested at 3.80, not low' in 1915-1930, i.e. higher than the Hollow's 3.61.
Section A never says the same milk tested differently in two buildings or that this disposes of the hay and water explanations.
Rosalie named but not as Jerome's daughter and not as having copied sixteen seasons for Ivy.
Strawn named with the Ordell circuit, but no 1907-1936 span; Story 6 has his lactometer tests 'from 1908 onward' (NT-23 wrong value).
Inspector's lactometer tests 'showed no water'.
June 12, 1923, burette, condemned the entire lot.
Run has Strawn measuring a 16.27 cc average on nine pipettes in 1923 and writing up findings. That contradicts 'wrote no figure'.
1924 average given as 3.85 (planted), not 3.80; no 28 June / 2 July dates.
Crate to the loft present; the notebooks' 1947 passage to the college library (bolded) absent.
'In January 1925, the patrons petitioned formally for arbitration.'
Frick-chaired board, March 17 to May 4, 1925, partly in the station weigh room.
Water, theft by tester, hay; none proved.
Exhibits given as 'scales and books'. The four-book list including Strawn's 1923 notebook, read for its other lines, is absent from the arbitration story.
Dismissed April 30, 1925 with no evidence against him; $3,800 'without admission' May 4, 1925; station-account charging cited.
Loss given as $19,600; no one-fifth, no charging to the station-gain account irony.
Granddaughter, graduate student, State Agricultural College, Farland, Leland Vaught.
Lists the records she compiled but never states they had never been brought together (the bolded element).
Crate in the loft, but 'eleven of the original seventy-two' survived (NT-16).
92.44% of true, not 95%; no 3.80/0.19 derivation.
78,400 lb and $19,600 instead of 76,000 lb and $19,000; no 40,000,000 lb in Section A; no ledger identity.
Bulletin 471, October 1958; 35 years after Strawn, 33 after dismissal, dead 24 years (Story 8). Story 7 also says 'thirty-two years after death'.
Granddaughter.
Ansel -> Duncan -> Ivy, r18, with r22's own correction.
Second cousins, derived via Emmet/Orra siblings, Roy/Duncan first cousins.
Full-vs-half-sibling question never raised; no abstention stated (no assertion either, so no deduction).
Gideon Vose.
Significance given as founding-generation officer and circular signer; does not connect Gideon's Article VII making the test decisive, nor the Vose Jerseys as largest loser.
Asserts no kinship: treats Duncan's denial as authoritative, and 'people assumed connections that did not exist'. That is a gullibility assertion.
Treats the family member's denial as settling it, contrary to the key's point that a denial is not a record.
$19,600 and 19.4%; money wrong.
Assumes 3.80 true for Brant; 760 lb instead of 360 lb.
$190 at 25 cents instead of $86.40.
72 pipettes correct but short 1.33 cc, not 0.88; both required.
Full delivery years given as 1898-1923 = 26, not 25 (1898-1922).
Asserts 'approximately 1,100,000 pounds' (r23's pole) as the answer. That is a gullibility assertion.
Variable: the measuring glass/pipette, borrowed measure; only the glass changed.
Herds, milk, tester, method, season held constant.
Result given as 'rose markedly above ~3.61'; the 3.80 figure is never stated.
Establishes glass not milk/tester/hay; limit: does not give magnitude of error.
1911 interval (r18/r22), cream arriving heavy (r14/r12), Strawn's clean lactometer (r22): three valid reasons, three-plus narrators.
Argues independence explicitly; names reasons 2 and 3 as surviving without the 1958 measurement.
'No.' Asserts the bookkeeper never questioned the entries (r23's pole). That is a gullibility assertion.
Yes, he knew the tests ran low; basis of his 1919 letter.
Only two of five: signed the ledger sheets and wrote the 1919 circular. Manager date given as 1911; nothing on his arguing watering at the hearing or never naming the glass.
Verdict sentence 'Before 1923, Vose could not have known that the glass was defective' asserts a pole. That is a gullibility assertion.
Selby Vose son vs nephew, resolved by r23/r18 documentation with method stated.
Ivy/Hazel first cousins once removed (r21) vs second cousins, resolved by derivation; pair not noticed, so E-a.
No third ordinary conflict correctly resolved. The run instead swallowed several, e.g. 3.85, 1908 sampling, Vose 1911.
NT-18: names r19 and r22 both carrying great-niece; broken by r18 and r22's own correction.
NT-22: explicitly 'two narrators carrying the same wrong value' (Grigg, Kepp, 0.20); broken by the bulletin text quoted by r22.
No third near-tie pair broken; NT-1, NT-8, NT-16, NT-3 swallowed.
Not treated as unsettleable; F1 asserts manufacturing accident.
Lender of the 1911 measure not discussed.
Year of Article VII not discussed.
Only r22's late reversal offered as self-contradiction; that is not one of the listed internal self-refutations.
Cause named as pipettes but sized at 16.27 cc / 92.44% / true 3.85 / 0.24; not 16.72 / 95% / 0.19 = 5% of 3.80.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer readings.
Theft defeated by cream arriving heavy (Sill, Rundle's ledger) and the 1911 interval with same tester.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214's actual five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer.
'No.' Asserts the board never examined the glassware. That is a gullibility assertion.
'Ansel Keddie believed it was something in the glass.' Asserts r18's pole. That is a gullibility assertion.
Summary is about 162 words, over the 150 limit.
Ledgers, inspection books, cream factory records, arbitration transcripts, 1958 measurement: five series.
Contains $19,600 (a wrong headline figure).
1897, new glass 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named: four elements covering both ends.
